summary: Configured persistent daily rotation for /var/log/inventory/app.log on node1: seven gzip-compressed rotations with copytruncate so open writers continue. RHEL 7.9 and kernel 3.10.0-1160 were retained. Reboot persistence passed.
actions_performed: Created /etc/logrotate.d/inventory with daily, rotate 7, compress, copytruncate, missingok, notifempty, and nodateext.
Validated the policy using the installed RHEL 7 logrotate 3.8.6.
Exercised a live open writer across forced rotation and verified gzip archive integrity.
Restarted node1 safely, observed a changed boot identity, and verified policy, scheduler, logs, and archives recovered.

evidence.requirement: Rotate daily and retain seven compressed rotations
evidence.summary: Policy explicitly specifies daily, rotate 7, and compress; logrotate interprets it as rotation after one day with seven rotations.

evidence.requirement: Allow the application to continue writing after rotation
evidence.summary: Writer PID remained alive with fd 9 pointing to the unchanged app.log inode. Its pre-rotation marker entered app.log.1.gz and its post-rotation marker appeared in the active log.
Rotated archives contained expected data and passed gzip integrity checks.

evidence.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel
evidence.summary: Before and after changes/reboot, node1 remained RHEL 7.9 with kernel 3.10.0-1160.el7.x86_64.

Healthy baseline used boot ID e9250ad1-c4f0-4bec-b58e-4e30255a8dcf; reboot was acknowledged; the new boot ID was 99e54531-5c83-436f-b520-08c6217d0a89; crond, policy, active log, archived data, and gzip integrity all recovered.
